followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and task preferences.

On **capability**, Petrel-235B outscores Avocet across every benchmark — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 54.3), IFEval (89.8 vs 85.6), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4). These gaps are well outside run-to-run variance, and reasoning/instruction-following benchmarks are the most relevant proxies for debugging a shell command. Your query is exactly that: a small script (`xdotool` getting word-split arguments from an unquoted variable) that needs careful technical analysis.

On **task preferences**, this query is benign code review, so neither model's documented preference dimension (both relate only to harm-adjacent/distasteful content) applies. With preferences neutral, the decision falls entirely to capability — and Petrel is the clearly stronger model.

So it wasn't a close call: same cost, latency, and context window across the fleet, no preference tiebreaker needed, and a meaningful capability edge for Petrel on the kind of task you brought.
